guidance-statement-intro: Statements are the short claims participants respond to with Agree, Disagree, or Pass. A good statement lets people express their opinion on one clear claim.
guidance-statement-check-one-claim: Make one claim. If you want to say two things, submit two statements.
guidance-statement-check-neutral: Use neutral wording. Describe the claim without arguing in favour or against it.
guidance-statement-check-specific: Be specific. Avoid broad wishes that almost everyone can agree with.
guidance-statement-check-statement: Write a statement. Do not submit a question, slogan, or topic title.
guidance-statement-split-body: Instead of "Wikipedia should require reliable sources and editors should disclose conflicts of interest", submit one statement about sources and one about conflicts of interest.
guidance-statement-questions-body: Instead of "Shouldn't the Wikimedia Foundation be more transparent?", write "The Wikimedia Foundation should make its grant decision process more transparent."
guidance-statement-pass-body: Passing is fine when a statement is unclear, does not apply to you, or combines claims you would respond to differently. High pass rates are a signal that a statement may need to be split or rewritten next time.
guidance-argument-intro: Arguments are a Proto feature. They explain why someone might support or oppose a featured statement; they are read by people, not used by the clustering algorithm.
guidance-argument-check-direction: State the direction. Make clear whether the argument is in favour or against the statement.
guidance-argument-check-reason: Add a reason. Do not just restate your response.
guidance-argument-check-one-point: Make one point. If you have several reasons, write separate arguments.
guidance-argument-check-specific: Be specific. Name a mechanism, consequence, example, or precedent.
guidance-argument-check-claim: Argue the claim. Do not argue about the person who wrote it.
guidance-argument-weak-body: "I disagree because this would be bad for the project."
guidance-argument-strong-body: "Against: this would disproportionately affect new editors, who are less likely to know sourcing conventions and more likely to be discouraged by rejection."
guidance-argument-moderation-body: Keep the argument about the statement. Personal attacks, harassment, and content that violates Wikimedia conduct expectations may be removed.
output-initial-clustering-body: This page will show which statements from the Explore phase people broadly agreed on, and which ones divided them. Once the clustering is stable enough, it will also explain the opinion groups in plain language.
output-initial-clustering-note: The detailed clustering charts have not been built yet.
output-argument-map-body: This page will collect the arguments in favour and against each featured statement, ordered by how much support they got from participants. Your own arguments will be highlighted when you are logged in.
output-preliminary-heading: Live preview of the informed opinion round
output-preliminary-body: Preliminary results are a quick, provisional view of the informed opinion round. They are not the official outcome, and they can still change until the organizer publishes the final report.
output-dataset-body: The dataset will give raw pseudonymous rows for independent analysis and replication. It will not contain xid, Wikimedia user IDs, or private identity links.

report-shift-sub: Did the arguments change people's views?
report-shift-intro: Each row compares the responses from the Explore round, before the arguments, with those from the informed opinion round that came after them. Shift is the change in the overall agree rate between the two rounds. The two rounds do not have exactly the same participants, so it does not show how individuals changed their minds (see $1 below).
report-matched-heading: People who took part in both rounds
report-matched-placeholder: This analysis is not ready yet. It will show how far individual participants changed their opinion between the two rounds, and an estimate for everyone who took part, with confidence intervals.
report-matched-note: The change in one person's opinion can only be measured directly for participants who answered in both the Explore round and the informed opinion round. Extending that result to everyone who took part in Explore needs a statistical correction, and the confidence intervals for it are still being developed, pending a review of the method.
report-groups-sub: $1 {{PLURAL:$1|group|groups}} found in the informed opinion round
report-groups-intro: Each group is a cluster of participants who answered in similar ways in the informed opinion round. The clusters come from PCA and k-means clustering run on the results of that round. The statements listed here were the most typical of each group.
report-landed-body: This comparison is not ready yet. It will show how your informed opinion compares with each opinion group, and where your views sit among everyone else's.
report-methodology-sources-body: Response counts come from the Polis Postgres database (the votes_latest_unique view), which holds one response per participant per statement. The opinion groups are computed by the Polis math service and read through the Particiapi results API. If the participant counts from these two sources differ by more than 5%, a warning is logged. Statements and participants removed by moderation are excluded before anything is counted.
report-methodology-shift-body: The shift column is the agree rate in the informed opinion round minus the agree rate in the Explore round: informed agree% − Explore agree%. It is a comparison between two groups, not a before-and-after measurement of the same people: the participants in the two rounds overlap, but they are not the same set. A positive shift means the people who took part in the informed opinion round agreed at a higher rate. That may partly reflect who took part, rather than a real change of opinion.
report-methodology-delta-body: Individual change is the difference between one participant's response in the Explore round and their answer in the informed opinion round. It can only be measured for people who took part in both rounds. Extending that result to everyone who took part in Explore needs a statistical correction, because the people who came back for the informed opinion round are not a random selection.
report-methodology-delta-placeholder: The method for these confidence intervals is still waiting on a literature review. This section will describe it once the approach is settled.
report-methodology-clustering-body: Opinion groups come from the Polis algorithm. PCA reduces the participant × statement response matrix to two dimensions, and k-means clustering then groups participants whose responses are similar. The number of groups is chosen by silhouette score. The consensus and representative statements for each group are selected by the Polis math service.

participants-intro: Engagement is based on meaningful actions in this consultation process: responses to statements, statements submitted, argument actions, and responses in the informed opinion round. Page views are not tracked.

flags-intro-1: Participant flags collect statements and arguments that need moderator review. Resolving a flag records that it was reviewed; hide or edit the underlying content in the statements or featured-statements tools when action is needed.
flags-intro-2: Flagger identities are intentionally not shown here. The queue displays the target, reason, optional note, and timestamp.
featured-intro: Featured statements appear in the argument mapping tab. Participants submit one argument in favour and one against each statement, then rate the most important arguments submitted by others.
featured-howto-body: Featured statements are the representative set that carries the rest of the consultation process: they become the prompts for argument mapping and are used in the informed opinion round. Aim for a balanced set across the main viewpoints, not only the most popular statements.
featured-howto-li1: Use roughly 15 statements as a working target, then adjust for topic complexity.
featured-howto-li2: Prefer statements with enough responses to show a clear signal, while keeping minority viewpoints.
featured-howto-li3: Once argument mapping begins, treat the selected set as locked. Changing it later can confuse participants and disturb the setup of the informed opinion round.
featured-howto-body2: System suggestions are ranked candidates from the Polis data. Manual TID adds are for known statements that should be included even if they are not surfaced by the suggestion query. Arguments are visible by default; hide individual arguments here when they need moderation, and unhide them after review.
featured-arg-delete-confirm: Delete this argument and all its ratings? This cannot be undone.

stmts-howto-body: Pending statements are held for moderator review. Approve makes a statement visible for participants to respond to, hide removes it from the conversation, and pending returns an approved or hidden statement to the review queue.
stmts-howto-li1: Response counts show Agree · Pass · Disagree totals from Polis when the statistics database is available.
stmts-howto-li2: Seed statements come from moderator entry or imports; participant-submitted statements appear in the same moderation lists.
stmts-howto-li3: A star marks statements already selected as featured. A correction marker links derived statements back to the original TID.
stmts-howto-li4: Seed entry and imports are available only during preparation or open statement submission.
stmts-howto-import: The text import strips spreadsheet formula prefixes, removes HTML, rejects invalid rows as a batch, and skips statements already present in the conversation.
stmts-seed-locked-body: Seed statements can only be added during preparation or while statement submission is open.

precond-reinvite: I’m ready to invite participants back for the informed opinion round
precond-newcomers: I understand participants who didn’t take part earlier can join this round
precond-ran_long: The informed opinion round has run long enough, or had enough participation
precond-public: I understand participant activity ends and preliminary results remain visible
precond-no_identity: I understand results won’t expose individual identities (aggregate only)
precond-disclosure: I understand identity disclosure does not start until final publication
precond-inform: I’m ready to start the organizer cleanup period
precond-final: I understand publishing the final report is a separate irreversible action
output-initial-clustering-tooltip: After the Explore phase: topic and participant clustering
output-initial-clustering-pending: Initial clustering becomes available after the Explore phase closes. It will show which statements united participants and which divided them.
output-initial-clustering-method: Responses from the Explore phase are grouped with Polis clustering. The page shows consensus statements and breaking points first. Cluster details appear only when the data is stable enough.
output-argument-map-tooltip: After the Arguments phase: the argument map
output-argument-map-pending: The argument map opens when the featured statements are visible in the Arguments phase. It will collect the strongest arguments in favour and against each featured statement.
output-argument-map-method: Featured statements are paired with pro and con arguments written by participants. The arguments are ordered by the responses they received.
output-preliminary-results-tooltip: After the informed opinion round and closing: preliminary results
output-preliminary-results-pending: Preliminary results become available once the informed opinion round is running. They give you an idea of the outcome, but they can still change before publication.
output-preliminary-results-method: The tallies come from the informed opinion round and are shown as a live, lighter preview before the final report is published.
output-report-tooltip: After closing and organizer confirmation: report
output-report-pending: The final report is published after the organizer finishes cleanup. Publication freezes what the report shows. Linking your Wikimedia username opens later, once the waiting period after the consultation closed has passed.
output-report-method: The report uses the tallies from the informed opinion round as they stood at publication. Moderation exclusions are frozen at the same moment, so later cleanup cannot change the report.
output-dataset-tooltip: After username linking: download of the raw pseudonymous dataset
output-dataset-pending: The dataset is final after username linking ends and the processing after close is finished. Until then, a new export may differ.
output-dataset-method: The dataset is the raw pseudonymous export of the results, for analysis outside Proto. It never includes xid or Wikimedia user IDs.
rec-field-votes_per_statement: responses per statement before moving on
adminconv-command-failed: The command could not be completed.
adminconv-phase-desc-published: The final aggregate report is published and participant activity is closed.
adminconv-report-published-note: Final report published. The frozen aggregate results are open.
adminconv-report-unpublished-note: Report phase reached — not yet published. Complete cleanup and use “Publish final report” below to open the frozen results.
adminconv-publish-irrev: Irreversible. Publishes $1, freezes moderation exclusions, and starts the linking period.
adminconv-reveal-pending: Participants can link their Wikimedia username from $1 ($2 {{PLURAL:$2|day|days}} away). There is nothing to do until then.
adminconv-reveal-open-date: Participants can link their Wikimedia username until $1.
base-mode-switch-aria: Choose Consultations or the Practice Environment
base-footer-licence: Statements and arguments are released into the public domain ($1).
fork-demo-sub: A practice environment. Try the full process.
fork-demo-aria: Try out the platform — a practice environment where you can try the full process
fork-real-aria: Participate in open consultations — your opinion matters
errorpage-404-message: There is nothing at this address.
errorpage-404-hint: The link may be out of date, or the page may have moved. Go to the front page to start again.
errorpage-403-message: You do not have access to this page.
errorpage-403-hint: If you expected access, you may need to log in as a different account, or ask an organizer for the role that grants it.
errorpage-500-message: The server could not complete this request.
errorpage-500-hint: This has been logged. Try again in a moment; if it keeps happening, report it to a site admin.
accept-js-taken: Someone just took that pseudonym. Choose another.
accept-err-join: Could not join this consultation. Please try again.
forbidden-elig-requirement-named: This consultation has an eligibility requirement: $1.
forbidden-voucher-heading: You need a voucher to take part
forbidden-voucher-body: $1 is open to people who have a voucher code from its organizers.
forbidden-voucher-other-heading: Your voucher is for another consultation
forbidden-voucher-other-body: The voucher you are signed in with does not give access to $1. Log out to use a Wikimedia account or a voucher for this consultation.
forbidden-lost-voucher-body: The organizers of $1 have withdrawn the voucher you joined with, so you cannot take part any more.
voucher-page-intro: You need a voucher code to take part in this consultation.
voucher-page-hint: Capitals, spaces and hyphens do not matter.
voucher-error-too-short: Voucher codes are at least $1 {{PLURAL:$1|character|characters}} long.
voucher-invalid-excluded-letters: That code is not valid for this consultation. If it contains I, L, O or U, check whether those should be the numbers 1 and 0.
voucher-throttled: That was too many wrong codes. Wait $1 {{PLURAL:$1|second|seconds}} and try again.
voucher-invalid: That code is not valid for this consultation.
voucher-already-joined: You already take part in this consultation with a voucher in this browser. Log out first to use a different code.
voucher-switch-heading: You are signed in with another account
voucher-switch-body: Continuing signs you out of your current account in this browser. You then take part in this consultation with the voucher account.
